text:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service:api-embeddings error_rate 5m avg > 8% in prod-east
maria: paging @oncall — getting a flood of 5xx on api-embeddings, started ~10:12 UTC. Customer-facing errors spiking. Not sure if rollout or infra.
raj: acked — I'm on it, joining bridge now. Can anyone confirm if there was a model rollout around 10:00?
emily: I saw a small model swap at 09:58 for canary traffic, should be limited to 5% but maybe routing borked.
oliver: joining. quick check: infra shows increased KV cache evictions on prod-east g4-pool around 10:06.
james: looking at logs, many requests failing with 502 followed by "decoder: OOM during attention" in GPU worker logs.
raj: ok that points to model memory pressure combined with request fanout. mitigation plan: 1) temporarily block canary traffic -> route all to stable 2) increase replica count for embeddings-service in prod-east 3) enable soft-fail fallback to smaller model for higher latency requests
maria: doing routing change now: applying policy to send canary->stable. pinging infra to scale.
ops-bot: Deploy Router Policy updated (policy-id: rp-1143). Traffic routing change applied.
oliver: scaling up replicas + warm workers. Will watch health.
emily: verifying canary traffic is zero now — looks good.
james: we've reduced OOMs but still seeing sustained ~3% 5xx. Might be residual KV cache thundering.
raj: enabling quick KV cache backoff + prefix caching for popular keys to reduce load.
monitoring-bot: Metric alert suppressed for 15m while we mitigate (suppression ticket: sup-792). Anyone object?
sara: no objection. we need to track customer impact though — product asked for counts.
maria: product: estimated 1.2k failed requests affecting ~40 orgs between 10:12-10:45, top affected accounts: acme-inc, beta-studio (internal anonymized list shared privately).
emily: sending a short status note to customer-ops with ETA for full recovery.
raj: incident contains: probable cause = model change + unexpected memory pressure + cache eviction storm. Immediate mitigations applied. Next: schedule post-incident review and remediation tasks.
maria: can we get a postmortem slot tomorrow? Suggest 11:00 UTC, 60m. @ops-bot can you create the postmortem thread & calendar invite?
ops-bot: Postmortem created: PM-1923456789. Calendar invite sent to participants.
james: initial action items (quick wins):
- revert canary routing logic to add stricter isolation (owner: eng-runtime)
- add temporary alert suppression config for the noisy 5xx alert to avoid pager noise during mitigation (owner: eng-sre)
- add fallback path to smaller-quantized model on OOM (owner: eng-ml)
raj: medium/long term items:
- add synthetic KV cache pressure test in CI that simulates eviction storm (owner: eng-infra)
- tune model memory estimator and auto-scale policy (owner: eng-runtime)
- add a dashboard for decoder OOM traces with sample IDs and request payload sizes (owner: eng-ml)
maria: can we also adjust paging policy: the current rule pages on 5m avg > 5% which caused noisy pages during cascade. Proposal: change to burn-rate-based trigger that accounts for customer-impact weight and SLO breach forecast.
oliver: i like burn-rate. concrete: page when projected SLO breach within 60m AND 5xx > 2% for two consecutive 5m windows. That should reduce noisy pages from transient blips.
sara: agree. add a separate low-priority alert to #incidents-info for awareness instead of full page.
monitoring-bot: Example new alert rule suggested:
```
alert: HighErrorBurnRate
expr: predict_slo_breach(error_rate[5m], burn_rate_window=60m) > 0.6 and avg_over_time(error_rate[10m]) > 0.02
labels:
  severity: page
  team: eng-sre
annotations:
  summary: "Projected SLO breach for api-embeddings"
```
maria: also add an alert dedupe layer keyed by org-id + endpoint to avoid 1k identical pages when a shared downstream error happens.
james: yes — and add a per-org mute window if the org has an ongoing degradation incident to avoid repeated paging.
raj: i'll own the immediate alert rule rewrite and dedupe implementation. Target: PR by EOD today, roll to staging tomorrow.
emily: i'll coordinate customer comms and publish a brief post-incident note after the postmortem.
ops-bot: Action items tracked: PM-1923456789-A1..A7. Assigned to owners, due dates populated.
maria: thanks team. main takeaways: mitigate -> contain -> avoid noise (alert dedupe + burn-rate paging) -> fix root cause (model mem estimator + kv tests). We'll review in postmortem and convert long-term items to RFCs.
raj: logging follow-up: capture a small sample of failed requests (sanitized) and persist in S3 for analysis (owner: eng-telemetry).
oliver: i'll keep workers warm for another 30m and then scale down.
sara: noted. I'll update the oncall rotation doc with new paging policy once we agree in the postmortem.
monitoring-bot: Incident closed by raj at 11:05 UTC. Postmortem meeting scheduled for 11:00 UTC tomorrow. Reference PM-1923456789.
maria: closing thread here; feel free to add any notes to the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:"
